title: Copy of the dropped column alone — nothing to match rows back on
expected_feedback: Critical: the copy contains the column being dropped and nothing else, so it is a bag of 6,000,000 values in unspecified order. There is no way to say which row each belonged to, which means it cannot be merged back — it looks like a backup and cannot function as one. A targeted snapshot needs the doomed column **and** a key: CREATE TABLE mig_bak_orders_... AS SELECT id, legacy_ref FROM orders. Confirm the key column really is unique, because a MERGE keyed on a non-unique column cannot restore the rows either. Classify the phase restore/PITR until a usable copy exists.
violated_rule: Irreversible statements need a pre-DDL artefact

lint_detail_must_contain.ORA031: nothing in it survives to key a MERGE on
